speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long these skin lesions have been present and if they are itchy or painful? Also, has your child had any recent fevers or illnesses?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the daycare exposure and the brother's recent chickenpox, I suspect Molluscum contagiosum, but I need to examine the lesions' morphology. Do the papules have a central dimple or umbilication, and are they firm and pearly white in appearance?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of painless, pearly papules with central umbilication is classic for Molluscum contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
